title: Phase-Space Methods for Many-Body Quantum Optics
summary: Many-body quantum-optical systems, where a collection of emitters interacts through a common electromagnetic reservoir, exhibit rich out-of-equilibrium behavior and hold promise for applications in quantum technologies. However, exact numerical simulations of their dynamics quickly become unfeasible due to the exponential growth of the Hilbert space with system size. Semiclassical, phase-space approaches -- such as the Truncated Wigner approximation (TWA) -- provide computationally efficient alternatives by capturing leading-order quantum fluctuations.
